extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for approving an affidavit of resignation and excluding a practitioner on consent under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, including acknowledgment elements, publication/notice obligations, supervisory rules for suspended practitioners, and reinstatement consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary consent / no coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge that his consent is freely and voluntarily rendered and that he is not being subjected to coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page states (Affidavit item 1): 'His consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, and he is not being subjected to coercion or duress.' This is a required affirmation in an affidavit of resignation submitted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of OED investigation (37 C.F.R. § 11.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must be aware that the OED Director opened an investigation of allegations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit acknowledges awareness that an investigation was opened and that the investigation 'delved into and obtained information' about specified matters (item 2). The page references the investigation as a factual predicate to the affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement/disclosure of relevant factual background
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit should acknowledge relevant factual circumstances uncovered by the investigation (e.g., attorney of record status, active state bar membership, ownership of firm, hiring/supervision of a suspended practitioner, factual history concerning the suspended practitioner's actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order summarizes factual matters the investigation obtained: (a) attorney of record in USPTO filings; (b) active Illinois bar membership; (c)-(d) history of Christopher Haigh's suspension/disbarment and his presence in Caliber IP; (e)-(f) alleged failure to meet 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(e) requirements when hiring/supervising a suspended practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of rules governing suspended practitioners (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner may act as a paralegal for another practitioner before the USPTO only if the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(e) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order explains that under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(e) a suspended practitioner 'may act as a paralegal... provided certain requirements are met' and notes the allegation that Respondent did not ensure those requirements were met when hiring/supervising Mr. Haigh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of alleged violations of USPTO professional rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit (and the OED Director's position) should identify the specific provisions of the USPTO Code/Rules alleged to have been violated (here 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) and 37 C.F.R. § 10.47(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order states the OED Director was of the opinion Respondent violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) (conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice) and § 10.47(b) (aiding a suspended or excluded practitioner). This identification is part of the affidavit/record used to approve exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement presumption for future proceedings (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge that if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for purposes of determining the application, that the allegations set forth in the investigation are true and that he could not have successfully defended himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit item 4: Respondent 'acknowledges that... the OED Director will conclusively presume... that (a) the allegations regarding him... are true and (b) he could not have successfully defended himself against such allegations.' The order reiterates this as a reinstatement consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge and understanding of applicable regulations and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must certify that he has fully read and understands specified regulations (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60) and is aware of the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit item 5: 'He has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60, and is fully aware of the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion.' This is an express required acknowledgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must expressly consent to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit item 6 and Order item 2: 'He consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.' The Order states the exclusion 'shall be, and hereby is, approved' and 'commencing on the date of this Final Order.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's statutory/regulatory authority to approve exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director's authority to approve an affidavit of resignation and order exclusion on consent is grounded in 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order cites these statutes and rules as the basis for jurisdiction and authority to approve the affidavit and exclude Respondent from practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit of resignation must satisfy the requirements set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) for the Director to approve exclusion on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order states 'Based on the foregoing, the USPTO Director has determined that Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).' The document uses that compliance as basis to approve the affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must electronically publish the Final Order in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order items 3 and 4 direct publication: electronic posting at the OED Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp) and an Official Gazette notice that summarizes the action, allegations, and reinstatement-presumption language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 regarding supervision of non‑practitioners and suspended practitioners in USPTO practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item 5: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.' The order earlier explains the role of § 11.58(e) concerning suspended practitioners acting as paralegals and the allegations that those requirements were not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any reinstatement request
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent seeks reinstatement, he must comply fully with the procedures and requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item 6 directs: 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.' This ties to the earlier acknowledged reinstatement presumptions and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The exclusion from practice before the USPTO takes effect on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order item 2 states exclusion commences 'on the date of this Final Order.' The document is dated Dec 2, 2014, reflecting the effective date.
